evidence.title: A prospective clinical study detects no group-level post-exposure skill change
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: A three-phase registry study before, during and after computer-aided detection found no statistically detected group-level post-exposure upskilling or deskilling. Inexperienced endoscopists improved during assistance; individual outcomes varied. Observation period and measurement context: November 2021–June 2025; three Norwegian clinics, 13 endoscopists, 5,013 procedures.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-134: Full methods, results, discussion, limitations and conflicts

evidence.limitations: PDR-5 endpoint rather than histological adenoma detection; nonrandomized phases, case mix, one device and small clinician sample. Null significance is not equivalence or proof against all skill loss. No raw data or replication inspected.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Qualifies inevitable competency-decay claims. Differences from the Polish decline study prevent treating this as a direct refutation.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Competency decay
terms.definition: A decline in the human or organizational expertise needed to perform, verify, contest, or recover work that is repeatedly delegated to AI-enabled systems. It is especially consequential when skills needed for independent judgment are lost.

relationships.explanation: Provides bounded counterevidence to inevitable decline; different endpoints and designs prevent direct replication claims.
